learningObjectives: Explain the developmental sequence underlying neuronal migration.
Identify the principal cells, structures and signals involved in neuronal migration.
Connect neuronal migration to later cognition and behaviour.
Interpret clinical findings without treating development as deterministic.

anatomy.label: Ventricular zone
anatomy.detail: Many cortical projection neurons are generated near the ventricular surface.
anatomy.clinical: Abnormal proliferation or departure can affect both cell number and placement.

anatomy.label: Radial glia
anatomy.detail: Radial glial fibres span the developing wall and guide migrating neurons.
anatomy.clinical: Radial glia are active developmental organisers, not merely support cells.

anatomy.label: Radial migration
anatomy.short: Outward movement toward the cortical plate
anatomy.detail: Projection neurons travel outward, pause and settle into emerging layers.
anatomy.clinical: Errors can create ectopic neurons or abnormal cortical thickness.

anatomy.label: Tangential migration
anatomy.short: Long-range movement across the developing forebrain
anatomy.detail: Many interneurons migrate from ventral origins into the cortex.
anatomy.clinical: Excitatory–inhibitory balance depends partly on successful interneuron migration.

anatomy.label: Cortical plate
anatomy.detail: Neurons stop migrating and mature within layer-specific networks.
anatomy.clinical: Final laminar position shapes inputs, outputs and developmental vulnerability.

interaction.title: Neuronal Migration sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to follow development over time.

stages.label: Attach
stages.text: Migrating cells engage guidance scaffolds and cues.

stages.label: Settle
stages.text: Cells stop in layer- and region-appropriate positions.

quizBank.question: Radial glia are important because they:
options: Act as progenitors and migration scaffolds
quizBank.explanation: Radial glia both produce cells and guide migration.

quizBank.question: Many cortical projection neurons migrate in an:
quizBank.explanation: Earlier-born neurons settle deeper; later-born neurons migrate past them to more superficial layers.

quizBank.question: Many cortical interneurons reach the cortex through:
quizBank.explanation: Interneurons commonly migrate tangentially from ventral progenitor regions.

quizBank.question: Neuronal heterotopia means:
options: Neurons are located where they should not be
quizBank.explanation: Heterotopia is ectopic neuronal placement due to disrupted migration.

quizBank.question: Why is neuronal position clinically important?
options: Layer and region determine connectivity opportunities
Position matters only for blood supply
quizBank.explanation: Location constrains which inputs and outputs a neuron can form.
